findings.title: Non-Complete structured_output bypasses acquisition/prefix content bounds and depth validation
evidence: crates/rrx/src/execution/native_result.rs:225-255 only checks prefix bytes, text bytes and complete serialized receipt bytes; structured_output is forbidden for Complete but unrestricted for all other acquisitions.

crates/rrx/src/state/execution/native_results.rs:87-97 deserializes a <=2MiB body with generic decode and uses the same validate; no structured-content depth/decoded-content limit precedes returning the DTO.
Approved native-result-receipts-design.md section3 specifies 1MiB decoded answer bytes, depth32 and <=64KiB total safe model-content prefix for invalid/partial/overflow paths.
findings.actual_guard_condition: For acquisition Unsupported/Partial/Ambiguous/Overflow, text=None and answer_sha256=None satisfy the non-Complete branch even when structured_output contains a >1MiB string (and the total encoded body still fits 2MiB). A nested structured Value above depth32 but below serde default recursion limit also passes this validator. SQL body length and all indexed/ownership checks can remain valid; they do not close the content hole.
findings.impact: The claimed bounded reader can return content outside the approved acquisition/depth/prefix profile. Core is not connected at this stage, so this is a persisted DTO contract/read-validation defect, not evidence of an actual native input exploit or approval bypass.

The text-only initial stage may instead reject structured_output entirely until a separately qualified bounded representation path exists; do not preserve unrestricted structured content under Overflow or partial status.
